emergency.notes: Police and fire/ambulance use different numbers. English support is limited — ask hotel staff for help if possible.

travelAdvisory.summary: Exercise normal precautions in Japan. U.S. citizens should always exercise caution when traveling abroad.

travelAdvisoryUK.summary: Most visits to Japan are trouble-free. Japan is a safe country with low crime rates.

healthcare.costForTourists: Tourists pay full price without insurance. A basic clinic visit costs $50-150. Emergency room visits $200-800. Hospital stays $300-1,000/night. Dental visits $50-200.
healthcare.pharmacyAccess: Pharmacies (yakkyoku) are widespread. Many OTC medications available including pain relievers and cold medicine. Prescription drugs require a local prescription — foreign prescriptions are not accepted.
healthcare.hospitalNotes: Hospital quality is excellent. Most staff speak limited English — major hospitals in Tokyo, Osaka, and Kyoto have international departments with English-speaking staff. St. Luke's International Hospital (Tokyo) and AMDA International Medical Information Center can help locate English-speaking doctors.
healthcare.insuranceAdvice: Travel insurance strongly recommended. Japanese hospitals typically require upfront payment in cash or credit card — insurance reimbursement happens after. Medevac coverage recommended for remote areas.

controlledSubstances.note: Strictly prohibited under the Stimulants Control Act. Carrying even with a valid foreign prescription can result in arrest and imprisonment. There is no exemption process.
Prohibited as it contains stimulant precursors. Use alternative decongestants like phenylephrine.
Allowed in small quantities (up to 1 month supply) with a Yakkan Shoumei import certificate and doctor's letter.
All cannabis-derived products are illegal regardless of THC content. CBD oil, edibles, and topicals are prohibited.
Allowed with a Yakkan Shoumei import certificate. Must carry original prescription and doctor's letter. Maximum 1 month supply.
Some benzodiazepines are controlled. Allowed with Yakkan Shoumei for up to 1 month supply with documentation.

medications.generalAdvice: Japan has some of the strictest drug import laws in the world. A Yakkan Shoumei (import certificate) must be obtained from the Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare BEFORE travel for many common medications. Apply at least 2 weeks in advance. Carry all medications in original packaging with a doctor's letter.
medications.yakkanShoumei: Required import certificate for many medications. Apply online via MHLW (mhlw.go.jp) before travel. Processing takes 1-2 weeks.

scams.name: Kabukicho bar scam
scams.description: Friendly strangers (often other foreigners or attractive locals) invite you to a 'local bar' in Kabukicho. Drinks arrive with a bill of ¥100,000+ ($700+). Staff block the exit and may threaten violence.
scams.avoidance: Never follow strangers to bars. Only enter establishments you chose yourself. Avoid touts in Kabukicho, Roppongi, and entertainment districts.

scams.name: Fake monks / temple donations
scams.description: People in monk robes approach tourists, give a 'blessed' bracelet or charm, then aggressively demand ¥1,000-5,000 payment.
scams.avoidance: Politely decline unsolicited gifts. Legitimate monks do not solicit on streets. Say 'kekkou desu' (no thank you) and walk away.

scams.name: Roppongi nightclub overcharging
scams.description: Clubs in Roppongi add hidden charges, serve drinks spiked to make you drowsy, then charge your credit card thousands of dollars while you're incapacitated.
scams.avoidance: Avoid clubs promoted by street touts. Pay in cash, not cards. Watch your drinks at all times. Stick to well-reviewed, established venues.

scams.name: Taxi long-haul scam
scams.description: Unlicensed taxi drivers at airports take unnecessarily long routes, especially from Narita/Kansai airports. Bills can be 2-3x the normal fare.
scams.avoidance: Use only official taxi stands. Better yet, use trains (Narita Express, Haruka) which are faster and cheaper. If taking a taxi, agree on the fare beforehand or confirm the meter is running.

connectivity.simOptions: Pocket WiFi rental at airports (¥500-1,000/day from companies like WiFi Rental Japan). eSIM via Ubigi, Airalo, or Holafly ($5-15 for 1-5GB). Physical SIM from BIC Camera, Yodobashi, or airport vending machines.
connectivity.wifiAvailability: Free WiFi at convenience stores (7-Eleven, FamilyMart, Lawson), train stations, and many restaurants. Quality varies — often requires registration. Shinkansen has WiFi on most routes.
connectivity.bestOption: eSIM (Ubigi or Airalo) for most travelers — activate before arrival. Pocket WiFi if traveling in groups. Japan's 4G/5G coverage is excellent nationwide.

cultural.tipping: Do not tip. Tipping is not customary and can be considered rude or confusing. Service charges are included in prices.
cultural.dressCode: Remove shoes when entering homes, temples, ryokans, and some restaurants (look for a genkan/entryway). Cover shoulders and knees at shrines and temples. Business settings are formal.
cultural.greetings: Bow instead of handshake. Deeper bow = more respect. A slight head nod is fine for casual encounters. Avoid strong eye contact with strangers.
taboos: Sticking chopsticks upright in rice (funeral symbolism)
cultural.haggling: Not practiced. Prices are fixed everywhere including markets and small shops.

safety.lgbtSafety: Generally safe but limited legal protections. Same-sex marriage not recognized. PDA is uncommon for all couples. Discrimination is rare but LGBTQ+ visibility is limited outside Tokyo's Shinjuku Ni-chome.
safety.soloFemaleSafety: Very safe. Some train cars have women-only sections during rush hour. Groping (chikan) on crowded trains is a known issue — women-only cars are the safest option.
safety.notes: Japan is one of the safest countries in the world for tourists. Main risks are natural disasters (earthquakes are frequent), language barriers in emergencies, and strict drug laws.

practical.visaFreeCountries: US citizens: 90 days visa-free. UK, EU, Australia, Canada also visa-free for 90 days.
practical.bestTimeToVisit: March-May (cherry blossom season), October-November (autumn foliage). Avoid July-August (hot, humid) and Golden Week (late April-early May, very crowded).

hospitals.name: St. Luke's International Hospital
hospitals.notes: Best hospital for English-speaking tourists in Tokyo. Full international patient services.

hospitals.name: Osaka University Hospital
hospitals.notes: Major university hospital serving Osaka. International patient services available.

immediate: Drop, cover, and hold on — Japan has frequent earthquakes
Register with J-Alert on your phone for automatic earthquake/tsunami notifications
After major quake near coast: move to high ground immediately — do not wait for tsunami siren
Japan's buildings are earthquake-resistant — sheltering inside is usually safer than running out
Follow tsunami evacuation route signs (blue wave symbols) to nearest high ground
after: Follow NHK World English broadcasts for instructions
Do not return to coastal areas until JMA (Japan Meteorological Agency) issues all-clear
Register at evacuation centers for safety checks

immediate: Monitor JMA typhoon forecasts — Japan has very accurate 5-day track predictions
When Special Warning issued: shelter indoors in strongest room away from windows
Follow evacuation orders (hinan shiji) from local government immediately
Identify local evacuation center (hinanjo) before typhoon season
after: Stay indoors for several hours after typhoon passes — trailing side can be equally severe
Watch for mudslides in mountainous areas after heavy rain
